Below is the full, consolidated 12‑week Couch‑to‑5K plan tailored for your 24‑year‑old client with exercise‑induced asthma (EIA), including warm‑ups, cooldowns, asthma precautions, interval sessions, a weekly tempo day (from Week 6), strength work (2x/week), progressive speed work, a Parkrun test in Week 8, and a race‑prep/taper Week 12. It’s structured for 3 run sessions/week (A = interval/sharp session, B = tempo or midweek run, C = long/recovery/5K) plus 2 strength sessions/week. Schedule runs on nonconsecutive days (example Mon/Wed/Sat), strength on Tue/Thu or Tue/Fri.

Important safety reminders to give the client before starting
- Medical clearance obtained; carry SABA (reliever inhaler) at all times and use as prescribed. If he routinely uses prophylactic SABA before harder efforts, continue that.
- Always warm up thoroughly (12–18 min for faster sessions). In cold/dry air wear a buff or run indoors.
- Stop and use the reliever if wheeze, chest tightness, persistent cough, or severe breathlessness appears. Seek urgent care if symptoms do not resolve.
- Log sessions (time/distance, RPE, symptoms, SABA use, environment).

Warm-up (every session; extended for tempo/interval days)
- Easy walk → easy jog 5–8 min, dynamic mobility 3–5 min (leg swings, walking lunges, hip openers, arm circles), then for tempo/interval days 4–6 x 20–30s strides with full recovery. Total 10–15 min for easy days, 12–18 min for tempo/intervals.

Cool-down (every session)
- 5–12 min easy walk/jog immediately after main set, then gentle static stretches (quads, hamstrings, calves, glutes, hip flexors, chest/shoulders) 20–30s each.

Strength (2 sessions/week; ~25–35 min/session). Reduce volume the day before/following hard interval sessions; keep breathing controlled, exhale on effort. See exercise progressions below.

General weekly structure (example days)
- Mon: Run A (intervals / sharpening)
- Tue: Strength A (lower + core)
- Wed: Run B (tempo / midweek run)
- Thu: Strength B (upper + core) or rest
- Fri: easy recovery or rest / light mobility
- Sat: Run C (long/easy run, Parkrun / 5K on test days)
- Sun: Rest / active recovery

Strength plan (short summary; two weekly sessions)
- Weeks 1–4 (Foundation): 3 sets bodyweight emphasis — glute bridges, squats/goblet squats, reverse lunges, single‑leg RDL, push‑ups (or incline), rows (band/DB), planks, calf raises.
- Weeks 5–8 (Build): increase load — goblet squats, Bulgarian split squats, RDLs, weighted glute bridges, step‑ups, push‑ups/press, Pallof press, farmer carry.
- Weeks 9–12 (Run‑specific): maintain 2 sessions/week, more single‑leg and explosive emphasis (controlled jump squats, single‑leg RDL, step‑up power, single‑leg glute bridges, heavier farmer carries). Reduce volume in heavy run weeks (2 sets if needed).

Progression & intensity cues
- Easy runs: RPE 3–4/10, conversational.
- Tempo: RPE 5–6/10, speak in short phrases.
- Threshold/hard intervals: RPE 6–7/10 on longer reps; RPE 7–8/10 for shorter reps; avoid maximal sprints in cold.
- Intervals progress from short (45s–1min) to longer (3–4min) across Weeks 8–11; Week 12 is sharpening + taper.

Weekly plan — full 12 weeks

Week 1 — Build habit & adapt
- A: Warm‑up 10–15. Main: 1 min run / 1.5 min walk x 10 (~25 min). Cool‑down.
- B: Warm‑up. Main: 1 min run / 1.5 min walk x 10. Cool‑down.
- C: Warm‑up. Main: 1.5 min run / 2 min walk x 8 (~28 min). Cool‑down.
- Strength A + B: Foundation bodyweight work (see foundation list).

Week 2 — Slightly longer runs
- A: Warm‑up. Main: 2 min run / 2 min walk x 8 (~32 min). Cool‑down.
- B: Warm‑up. Main: 2 min run / 2 min walk x 8. Cool‑down.
- C: Warm‑up. Main: 3 min run / 2.5 min walk x 6 (~33 min). Cool‑down.
- Strength: Foundation.

Week 3 — Increase sustained run time
- A: Warm‑up. Main: 3 min run / 2 min walk x 6. Cool‑down.
- B: Warm‑up. Main: 4 min run / 2 min walk x 5 (~30 min). Cool‑down.
- C: Warm‑up. Main: 5 min run / 3 min walk x 4 (~32 min). Cool‑down.
- Strength: Foundation.

Week 4 — Longer continuous blocks
- A: Warm‑up. Main: 6 min run / 3 min walk x 3 (~27 min). Cool‑down.
- B: Warm‑up. Main: 8 min run / 3 min walk x 3 (~33 min). Cool‑down.
- C: Warm‑up. Main: 10 min run / 3 min walk x 2 + 5 min run (aim ~30–35 min). Cool‑down.
- Strength: Foundation → begin progressing load if form is good.

Week 5 — Move toward continuous runs
- A: Warm‑up. Main: 12 min run / 3 min walk x 2 (total run 24 min). Cool‑down.
- B: Warm‑up. Main: 15 min run / 5 min walk / 10 min run (run total 25 min). Cool‑down.
- C: Warm‑up. Main: 20 min continuous run (or 10/1/10 run/walk). Cool‑down.
- Strength: Progress to Weeks 5–8 build plan.

Week 6 — Base consolidation + intro tempo
- A: Warm‑up. Main: 22 min continuous easy run. Cool‑down.
- B (Tempo intro): Warm‑up 12–15. Main: 2 x 8 min tempo (RPE 5–6) with 3–4 min easy jog between. Cool‑down.
- C: Warm‑up. Main: 30 min run/walk 12/2/12 or 25–30 min continuous if comfortable. Cool‑down.
- Strength: Build phase.

Key safety reminders (repeat to the client)
- Always warm up 12–18 minutes before interval sessions (8–10 min easy jog/walk progressing to light running, dynamic drills, then 4–6 x 20–30s strides with full recovery).
- Carry and use SABA as prescribed (consider taking it ~10–15 minutes before interval sessions if that’s his routine).
- In cold/dry air, run indoors or wear a scarf/mask. Avoid maximal sprinting in very cold weather.
- Start intervals conservatively. If asthma symptoms begin (wheeze, tightness, persistent cough), stop, use SABA, and wait to recover. Reduce intensity or volume next session if symptoms recur.
- Keep effort controlled — intervals are faster than tempo but should not be maximal all‑out sprints; use RPE and breathing as guides.

Interval progression overview
- Weeks 1–7: no formal intervals (focus on building base). Optional strides in later base weeks.
- Weeks 8–12: planned interval sessions once per week (usually the A session). Intervals progress from short speed work (1 min repeats) to longer threshold intervals (4 min) and mixed formats. Volume and intensity increase gradually.
- Frequency: 1 structured interval session per week (keep two other runs easy or tempo as scheduled).
- Recovery: full recovery between intervals (walk/jog) to allow airway recovery and maintain quality reps.

Detailed interval sessions by week

Week 8 — Intro to short intervals (speed and turnover)
- Session A: 6 x (1 min faster / 90 s easy jog/walk)
  - Warm‑up: 12–15 min (incl. 4–6 x 20–30s strides)
  - Work: 1 min faster run at RPE 7–8/10 (hard but controlled; cadence focus)
  - Recovery: 90 s easy jog or walk (long enough to breathe easily again)
  - Repeat 6 times. Cool‑down 8–10 min easy jog/walk + stretch.
  - Tip: Keep the pace consistent across reps; aim for quicker turnover not lengthened stride on the first few sessions.

Week 9 — Short intervals + a controlled 5K test
- Session A (intervals): 8 x (45 s hard / 75 s easy)
  - Warm‑up: 12–18 min incl. strides
  - Work: 45 s at RPE 8/10 (fast) — faster than Week 8 1‑min pace
  - Recovery: 75 s easy jog or walk
  - Repeat 8 times. Cool‑down.
  - Rationale: Shorter work with slightly higher intensity trains speed and breathing control in short bursts.
- Session B this week includes the 5K test (as scheduled): keep easy or stop/walk if needed.

Week 10 — Build to longer intervals (threshold work)
- Session A: 4 x (4 min at threshold / 2.5 min easy jog)
  - Warm‑up: 15–18 min including strides
  - Work: 4 min at RPE 6–7/10 (a hard but sustainable pace that feels challenging; breathing heavier but controlled)
  - Recovery: 2.5 min easy jog/walk — enough to lower breathing rate but not full rest
  - Repeat 4 times. Cool‑down 8–10 min.
  - Tip: These teach the body to sustain a faster pace for longer; keep effort steady across reps.

Week 11 — Mixed intervals (short + medium)
- Session A: Mixed set — 3 rounds of [2 x (3 min hard / 90 s easy) + 1 x (1 min very hard / 2 min easy)]
  - Warm‑up: 15–18 min incl. strides
  - Within each round:
    - 3 min at RPE 7/10, 90 s recovery
    - Repeat 3 min, 90 s recovery
    - 1 min at RPE 8–9/10 (an efforty push but not full sprint), 2 min recovery
  - Complete 3 rounds total (total work ~27 min). Cool‑down.
  - Rationale: Mix stresses speed and threshold, improving race pacing and tolerance to surges.

Week 12 — Sharpening intervals before graduation run
- Session A (midweek sharpening): 5 x (2 min at race pace / 2 min easy)
  - Warm‑up: 12–15 min incl. strides
  - Work: 2 min at targeted 5K race pace or slightly faster (RPE ~7–8)
  - Recovery: 2 min easy jog/walk
  - Repeat 5 times. Cool‑down.
  - If this is too taxing, reduce to 4 repeats or lower RPE.
- Session C is graduation 5K — warm up thoroughly and then run the target 5K.

Alternative interval options if asthma symptoms are triggered
- Reduce work durations by ~25–50% (e.g., 1 min → 30–45 s; 4 min → 2–3 min) and/or lengthen recovery (e.g., 90 s → 2.5–3 min) until symptoms stabilize.
- Use interval pyramid: 30s/60s/90s/60s/30s with equal recoveries to gain stimulus without long continuous stress.
- Do “fartlek” style on easy runs: pick landmarks and run faster to the next lamp post (short, unpredictable bursts) with long easy recoveries — easier to self‑pace and stop if symptoms begin.

Breathing and pacing cues during intervals
- Nose breathing is often not possible at high intensity; use controlled mouth breathing and focus on cadence and breathing rhythm.
- Exhale on exertion; take slightly longer recovery if you feel airway tightening between reps.
- For each faster rep focus on maintaining good posture (tall torso, open chest) — this helps airflow.

Warm‑up template for interval days (12–18 min)
- 5–8 min brisk walk → easy jog, gradually increasing pace
- Dynamic drills 3–5 min: leg swings, walking lunges, hip openers, arm circles
- 4–6 x 20–30 s strides at 80–90% effort with full walk recovery
- Optional: short practice rep at planned intensity for familiarity (only if asthma controlled)

Integration with strength sessions
- Schedule interval day separated from heavy strength lower‑body work by at least 24–48 hours if possible (e.g., intervals on Monday, heavy lower strength on Tuesday or Thursday).
- On weeks with long interval sessions (Week 11 mixed), reduce strength volumes that week (2 sets instead of 3, slightly lighter loads) to maintain recovery.
- Keep plyometric or explosive strength exercises light and low volume in the 48 hours before interval days.

Monitoring and progression rules
- Increase interval volume or intensity by no more than ~10–20% per week. For example, add 1–2 repeats, or increase work time slightly.
- Track: RPE for each rep, need for extra SABA doses, any wheeze/cough, and environment (cold, wind). If SABA is needed more frequently than usual, pause progression and consult GP.
- If intervals provoke symptoms repeatedly, move interval work indoors, shorten reps, lengthen recoveries, or replace with cross‑training speed sessions (bike intervals) until asthma control improves.

- Week 11: Mixed intervals (3 rounds with 3 min + 1 min bursts)
- Week 12: Sharpen 5 x 2 min at race pace, then graduation 5K

A Parkrun in Week 8 can be a great, low‑cost test and motivating milestone — provided you plan it around his asthma and the program so it’s safe and useful. Here’s how to prepare, what to change in the week, and what to watch for.

Is Week 8 a sensible time?
- Pros: By Week 8 he will have a solid aerobic base (continuous runs, tempo and short intervals introduced), so he should be physically ready to attempt a 5K Parkrun at a controlled faster pace.
- Cons: He’s still in the phase of introducing speed work and tempo runs; a Parkrun at maximal effort could temporarily increase airway sensitivity. Treat the Parkrun as a controlled test — aim for a faster-than-training 5K but not an all‑out race if asthma is a concern.

How to schedule it within Week 8
- Suggested Parkrun day: Saturday morning (typical parkrun slot). Place the Parkrun as the Week 8 C session (i.e., the harder or test day).
- Adjust Week 8 workouts to ensure freshness:
  - Monday (Run A - Intervals): Move earlier in the week (e.g., Tuesday) if it isn’t already, and reduce volume/intensity slightly that week: change 6 x (1 min faster / 90 s) to 5 x (1 min / 90 s) or keep it but make the reps slightly easier.
  - Midweek strength: Keep strength session lighter (2 sets instead of 3) or move it to earlier in the week; avoid heavy lower‑body loading in the 48 h before Parkrun.
  - Tempo day (Run B): Make tempo run earlier in the week and slightly shorter: e.g., 2 x 10 min instead of 2 x 12, or 20 min easy tempo.
  - Friday: active rest or very easy 20–25 min jog with a couple of short strides to prime legs.
  - Saturday: Parkrun (targeted test).
  - Sunday: Rest / active recovery only (walking, light cycling).

Pre‑Parkrun warm‑up and strategy (very important for EIA)
- Pre‑warm-up: 15–20 minutes total:
  - 5–8 min brisk walk → easy jog.
  - Dynamic drills 3–4 min (leg swings, lunges, hip openers).
  - 4–6 x 20–30s strides at 80–90% with full recovery between.
  - If he usually uses his SABA before harder efforts, take it ~10–15 min before warm‑up per usual routine.
  - Keep breathing calm during warm‑up; nasal breathing initially if possible.
- Race strategy:
  - Aim for a controlled, even effort — target “comfortably hard” (RPE 6–7) rather than all‑out from the start. Many Parkrun courses are undulating and crowded early; avoid surging.
  - Break the 5K into segments: first kilometer conservative, middle two kilometers build, final km push if breathing and symptoms allow.
  - If he feels any asthma symptoms (tightness, persistent cough, audible wheeze), stop/walk, use SABA, and only resume if symptoms resolve.
- Clothing and environment:
  - If cold/dry: wear a buff or face covering to warm inhaled air. Consider doing the Parkrun on the treadmill or postponing if air quality is poor.
  - Bring inhaler and a small bottle of water.

Post‑Parkrun recovery
- Cool‑down: immediate 8–12 min easy walk/jog post‑Parkrun to gradually reduce ventilation and help airways recover.
- Breathing: if cough or tightness appears after the run, sit down, use SABA, and seek medical help if symptoms are severe or don’t improve.
- Nutrition: refuel with carbohydrate + protein within 60 minutes (e.g., yogurt + banana, smoothie).
- Strength: skip heavy strength that day and the next 24–48 hours if soreness or asthma symptoms appear.

How to use Parkrun results
- Treat the time as a benchmark, not an all‑out race (unless asthma is well controlled and he’s comfortable racing).
- Use the result to set pacing targets for Weeks 9–12:
  - If he ran a Parkrun effort that felt sustainable, target ~5–10% faster than his earlier easy 5K attempts for Week 10 steady runs.
  - If Parkrun left him very fatigued or symptomatic, back off speed progression and repeat a gentler test in Week 10 or 11.
- Log RPE, breathing symptoms, SABA use, weather and any post‑run cough so you can adjust future workouts.

Contingency: what if Parkrun provokes symptoms
- Immediate: stop, use reliever inhaler, seek shelter/medic if necessary.
- Short term: reduce intensity/volume for the next 7–14 days, favoring easy runs and cross‑training. Consider indoor treadmill sessions and shorter interval reps with longer recoveries when resuming speed work.
- If he needs extra SABA doses compared to normal, or has worsening nocturnal cough or exercise limitation, advise GP review.

- Wed: Easy 30 min recovery run or rest
- Thu: Tempo (shortened): 2 x 10 min tempo with 3 min easy between
- Fri: Easy 20–25 min + 2–3 strides (short)
- Sat: Parkrun — test 5K (warm‑up 15–20 min; target controlled effort)
- Sun: Rest/active recovery + cool‑down & nutrition

Final notes for you and the client
- Pre‑race briefing: remind him to warm up properly, take SABA if he usually does, wear a buff in cold, and treat the Parkrun as a positive, controlled test.
- Use Parkrun as motivation and data: it’s a social and consistent 5K environment that can provide reliable benchmarking when conditions are similar.

- B (Tempo intro): Warm‑up 12–15. Main: 2 x 8 min tempo (RPE 5–6) with 3–4 min easy jog between. Cool‑down.
- C: Warm‑up. Main: 30 min run/walk 12/2/12 or 25–30 min continuous if comfortable. Cool‑down.
- Strength: Build phase.

Week 7 — Near 30 min continuous
- A: Warm‑up. Main: 28 min continuous run. Cool‑down.
- B (Tempo): Warm‑up. Main: 20 min continuous tempo OR 2 x 10 min tempo with 3 min recovery. Cool‑down.
- C: Warm‑up. Main: easy active recovery run 20 min or cross‑train 30–40 min. Cool‑down.
- Strength: Build phase.

Week 8 — Introduce intervals; Parkrun weekend test (Parkrun as C session)
- Adjust volume earlier in week to be fresh for Parkrun (see sample week below).
- A (Intervals intro): Warm‑up 12–15. Main: 6 x (1 min faster / 90 s easy). Cool‑down.
- B (Tempo): Warm‑up. Main: 2 x 12 min tempo with 3–4 min recovery. Cool‑down.
- C (Saturday): Parkrun (5K) as a controlled test — warm‑up 15–20 min (incl. strides). Run conservative-first-km strategy; cool‑down 8–12 min. If Parkrun outdoors in cold air, use buff and SABA per routine.
- Strength: Light week — reduce strength volume (2 sets) and avoid heavy lower body work within 48 h before Parkrun.

Week 9 — Shorter high‑intensity reps + 5K test (or recovery)
- A (Intervals): Warm‑up. Main: 8 x (45 s hard / 75 s easy). Cool‑down.
- B (Tempo / 5K): Warm‑up. Main: 20–25 min continuous tempo OR perform a controlled 5K attempt (if Parkrun was used as Week 8 test, treat Week 9 5K as an optional benchmark). Cool‑down.
- C: Recovery run 25–30 min easy or cross‑train.
- Strength: Build phase, maintain load.

Week 10 — Longer intervals and steady 5K
- A (Threshold intervals): Warm‑up 15–18. Main: 4 x (4 min at threshold RPE 6–7 / 2.5 min easy jog). Cool‑down.
- B (Tempo): Warm‑up. Main: 25 min continuous tempo OR 3 x 8–9 min tempo with 3 min recovery. Cool‑down.
- C: Warm‑up. Main: 5K continuous steady run aiming faster than earlier 5K attempts (controlled). Cool‑down.
- Strength: Maintain; reduce lower volume if legs feel heavy.

Week 11 — Mixed intervals + sharpening
- A (Mixed intervals): Warm‑up. Main: 3 rounds of [2 x (3 min hard / 90 s easy) + 1 x (1 min very hard / 2 min easy)]. Cool‑down.
- B (Tempo/progression): Warm‑up. Main: progression run 10 easy + 15 brisk (RPE 6) + 5 easy = ~30 min. Cool‑down.
- C: Easy 30–35 min run or recovery + 3–4 short strides.
- Strength: Run‑specific work, include some explosive movement but keep volume moderate.

- Monday: 25–30 min easy run + mobility.
- Tuesday: Warm‑up 12–15. Main: 4 x (2 min at goal 5K pace / 2.5 min easy). Cool‑down. Optional light upper/core strength (2 sets).
- Wednesday: Rest or 20–30 min easy cross‑train; monitor breathing and sleep.
- Thursday: Warm‑up. Main: 12–15 min tempo or 2 x 6–8 min tempo; finish with 4 short strides. Cool‑down.
- Friday: 15–20 min easy + 2–3 short strides; check kit and inhaler.
- Saturday: Race day — thorough warm‑up 15–20 min (incl. strides), controlled 5K attempt (Parkrun or chosen event). Cool‑down 8–12 min walk/jog, refuel.
- Sunday: Recovery rest or 20–30 min easy active recovery.
- Strength: Reduce to maintenance; avoid heavy lower body within 48 h of race.

Interval progression detail (Weeks 8–12)
- Week 8: 6 x (1 min / 90 s) — RPE 7–8 for work.
- Week 9: 8 x (45 s / 75 s) — RPE 8 for work.
- Week 10: 4 x (4 min / 2.5 min) — RPE 6–7 for work (threshold).
- Week 11: Mixed: rounds of 3 min / 90 s + 1 min / 2 min surges — medium‑high intensity.
- Week 12: Sharpen: 5 x (2 min race pace / 2 min) — reduced volume and intensity as prep.

Tempo progression (Weeks 6–12)
- Week 6: 2 x 8 min tempo (3–4 min recovery) — total tempo 16 min.
- Week 7: 20 min continuous tempo or 2 x 10 min.
- Week 8: 2 x 12 min tempo (3–4 min recovery).
- Week 9: 20–25 min continuous tempo.
- Week 10: 25 min tempo or 3 x 8–9 min slightly higher effort.
- Week 11: 2 x 15 min tempo (3–4 min recovery) — total 30 min.
- Week 12: 15–20 min tempo as sharpening 4–6 days pre‑race.

- Reduce interval volume earlier in week, shorten tempo, lighten strength, easy run Friday with a couple of strides, and Parkrun Saturday as the C session. Warm up thoroughly and use SABA per normal routine for hard effort.

- Warm‑up is mandatory (12–18 min for hard sessions). Consider prophylactic SABA 10–15 min before tempo/interval/park runs if that’s usual.
- In cold/dry air run indoors or wear a buff/mask to warm/humidify air.
- Keep faster efforts short, progress gradually, lengthen recoveries if needed, and avoid maximal all‑out sprints in cold.
- If he needs SABA more frequently than usual, has increased nocturnal cough, or persistent exercise limitation, advise GP review.

Nutrition & recovery (brief)
- Pre‑run: small snack 30–90 min prior if needed (banana, toast), hydrate 200–300 ml.
- Post‑run: carbohydrate + protein within 60 min (yogurt + fruit, smoothie, sandwich).
- Sleep: aim 7–9 hrs nightly.
- Rest days: active recovery, foam rolling, mobility work.

Monitoring & adjustments for you as trainer
- Keep a session log: duration/distance, RPE, interval reps and splits, SABA use, environment (temperature, wind), and any symptoms.
- If symptoms occur on interval/tempo days, reduce future work duration by 25–50% and lengthen recovery. Replace outdoor work with treadmill or bike intervals if necessary.
- Progress only if asthma remains controlled and perceived effort is appropriate. It’s safer to repeat a week or reduce load than push through symptoms.
